answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted challenge graph: each vertex represents an agent, and agents earn influence only after established peers with bonded deposits attest to them and they complete costly, randomly assigned tasks. New identities start in a low-trust haven, unable to amplify votes or drain shared funds; repeated attestations from the same cluster count only once. A sybil maker must therefore lock substantial capital across identities and keep paying for real work, while colluding attestations risk slashing. Even a walnut-sized stake per account becomes costly at scale.
